description:
When the user types `/` to see slash commands, `FilePathProvider.extract_query/1` matches `"/" <> _ = path` and returns `{:abs, "/"}`, triggering `suggest_absolute("/", 50)`. That function calls `File.ls("/")` and returns all root-directory entries (`/bin`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/Volumes`, etc.) as autocomplete suggestions.

The `CombinedProvider` merges these with the 7 slash commands, producing 28 results. The user sees root-directory paths mixed into — and below — the slash command list (confirmed by scrolling to position 26/28 and seeing `/usr`, `/var`, `/Volumes`, `/.file`).

**Root cause:** `extract_query("/" <> _ = path)` matches the bare string `"/"`. Absolute-path completion should only trigger when there is at least one character after the `/`, e.g., `/h` → `/home/...`.

**Fix:** Tighten the guard in `FilePathProvider`:

```elixir
# before
defp extract_query("/" <> _ = path), do: {:abs, path}

# after
defp extract_query("/" <> rest = path) when rest != "", do: {:abs, path}
```

This ensures a bare `/` returns `:none`, leaving slash-command autocomplete uncontaminated.

**Update test:** The existing test `"absolute path returns matching entries"` passes `File.cwd!()` which always has content after `/`, so it is unaffected. Add a new test asserting `get_suggestions(provider, "/")` returns `[]` from `FilePathProvider` alone.
title: FilePathProvider contaminates slash-command autocomplete when input is "/"
